feeds_status:
**TODAY'S ideas-feeds ACTION SUCCEEDED, AND IT LANDED AT 19:57 IST — WHILE THIS ROUTINE WAS MID-RUN.** That breaks a three-day cancellation streak and it also invalidated several of this run's own conclusions, which are corrected throughout this log. Run **44313598476** committed `f0345e90df` "Daily Ideas feeds 2026-11-18 19:57 IST": `feeds_status.json` built **2026-11-18 19:56 IST**, **128 files landed, 0 refused**, `steps_failed: ['wpi']` only, and just three hosts blocked (tradestat, metalbook, westmetall). It finished in about 61 minutes — inside the 90-minute cap, but only just.

**The three preceding days did fail, and the mechanism is worth keeping on record because the margin is thin.** Measured from the Actions API during this run:

| run | date | started → ended (UTC) | wall | conclusion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 43227180887 | 2026-11-12 | 13:25:38 → 14:27:34 | 62 min | success |
| 43433543004 | 2026-11-13 | 13:25:38 → 14:56:02 | 90 min | **cancelled** |
| 43875640839 | 2026-11-16 | 13:25:39 → 14:56:02 | 90 min | **cancelled** |
| 44092608136 | 2026-11-17 | 13:25:39 → 14:56:04 | 90 min | **cancelled** |
| 44313598476 | 2026-11-18 | 13:25:40 → ~14:26 | ~61 min | **success** |

On 17-Nov steps 1–18 all finished by 13:48:52Z (23 minutes in — PIB, every commodity host, WPI, trade, universe, scan, signals, scorecard), then **step 19 "Order-book ledger refresh" ran 13:48:52Z → 14:50:09Z, 61 minutes on its own**, and step 20 was killed at the cap before step 26 "Commit the feeds". So on each cancelled day a complete day's feeds was built and discarded.

**The risk has not gone away just because today worked.** The successful runs took 62 and ~61 minutes against a 90-minute cap, and the single step that decides it took 61 minutes by itself on 17-Nov. A slow BSE evening tips it again. The durable fixes remain, cheapest first: raise `timeout-minutes` above 90; split the order-book refresh into its own scheduled workflow so it cannot starve the commit; and — the real defect — **move the commit so that whatever HAS been built lands even when a later step is killed**, since steps 1–18 produced a complete day's feeds on every one of the three failed days. `.github/workflows/ideas-feeds.yml` is outside this routine's permitted scope, so this is a recommendation, not a change made here.

**Consequence for this run, stated plainly as a process lesson.** This routine read the committed panels at 19:43–19:45 IST, when they were still the 2026-11-12 build, and reached conclusions from them — that the commodity panel was four trading days stale and that the government lane was dark. The Action replaced those files at 19:57 IST with today's data. The run therefore had to merge origin/main mid-flight and redo the commodity and updates lanes. **A future run should check whether the Action has landed before trusting a stale stamp, or simply wait for it** — the routine fires at 14:00 UTC and the Action commits around 14:26.

govt_considered.verdict: **A real quiet day, measured rather than assumed.** The Action's `govt.py` run (built 2026-11-18 18:57 IST) scanned 41 PIB English releases, opened 5 and kept 0. The gate's own breakdown: 30 carried no decision verb, 4 were noise, 4 were below the ₹1,000 cr floor, 2 were backgrounders and 1 was in a sector with no basket. On the playbook's own evidence this is the correct and most common answer, and no bar was lowered to manufacture an idea.

govt_considered.release: Ministry of Commerce & Industry — "Department of Commerce Amends Guidelines of Four Interventions under Export Promotion Mission to Enhance Support" (outlay ₹25,060 cr, the day's only unmapped release)
govt_considered.verdict:
**Not actionable, and no name added to `theme_map.json` — the measured history is the whole reason.** ₹25,060 cr is a large number, but the question this page asks is not how big it is: it is **whose order book it lands in**. An export-promotion mission that *amends guidelines of four interventions to enhance support* is assistance paid to exporters — it widens eligibility and subsidy, it does not procure anything. That is structurally the PM Surya Ghar pattern, the one programme in the measured table that **underperformed outright** (basket 1.8x against the market's 2.0x, 0% made 5x), precisely because a household or firm-level subsidy is not an order book. The programmes that paid — defence indigenisation 17.4x, shipbuilding 16.2x, RDSS smart meters 12.0x — all turned into procurement someone had to win.

There is also nothing to verify a company against. The playbook's rule for an unmapped release is to search the universe, confirm materiality from the company's own filings, and add the name with the document read in the `why`. A guidelines amendment names no beneficiary and awards no contract, so any name added would be a hunch, which the rule forbids. **Revisit only if the mission is later tied to specific procurement or capacity building.**

govt_considered.release: Ministry of Heavy Industries — "MHI receives 22 bids for 10 GWh Advanced Chemistry Cell manufacturing capacity under PLI ACC Scheme" (₹18,100 cr, carried in the superseded 2026-11-12 build)
govt_considered.verdict: **Considered and deliberately not acted on; superseded by today's build but recorded because this run read it.** It is a *receipt of bids*, not an award: 22 bids for 10 GWh, no winner named, nothing yet in anybody's order book. With no allocation announced there is no filing against which to verify materiality, so adding names would be the hunch the rule forbids. The adjacency is in any case already covered — `theme_map.json` carries `bess` (31 names) and `critical_minerals` (13), and the gate's own `body_mentions` matched this release to BESS, solar/KUSUM and pumped storage; it scored `theme_in: null` only because the title names no mapped sector. **Revisit when MHI announces the allocation**, when the winners are nameable and an `acc_cells` theme can be built from their filings.

**Two rows checked against the companies' own filings this run — one CONFIRMED, one a misread. The ledger goes from 51 to 53 rows** (`orderbook_jumps.json` built 2026-11-18 21:55 IST), and `orderbook_verified.json` from 45 to 47.

### 1. Ganesh Infraworld Ltd (NSE:GANESHIN) — CONFIRMED, +70.0%, and the market has not followed

Both legs were opened and read. **Latest ₹3,845 cr as on 30-Sep-2026**: the press release filed 15-Nov-2026 is headed *"Ganesh Infraworld Reports Q2 & H1FY27 Results; **Consolidated Order Book Stands at 3,845 Cr as of Sept,2026**"* and repeats it in the highlights — explicitly consolidated, so company-wide. **Year-ago ₹2,262.3 cr as on 30-Sep-2025**: stated **twice** in the Q2 FY26 investor presentation filed 14-Nov-2025 — the CMD's desk (*"...with an order book of 2,262.3 crores"*) and the Company Snapshot slide, which sits beside *"Debt/Equity (As on September'25) 0.35x"* and so anchors the date — and corroborated at ₹2,262.0 cr in the same day's press release. A clean twelve-month span, filed almost exactly a year apart. **True YoY +70.0%.** The only definitional softness is that the 2025 figure does not say standalone or consolidated.

**Trigger: 14-Aug-2026**, the conference-call update stating ₹4,090.3 cr as on 30-Jun-2026 against ₹2,262.3 cr as on 30-Sep-2025, +80.8% — and said honestly, that pair spans nine months, not twelve, because the ledger holds no 30-Jun-2025 reading, so the trigger's own percentage is flattered by the shorter window even though it clears the bar either way.

**Two facts that cut against the row and belong on it.** The order book **fell** between trigger and latest, ₹4,090.3 cr (Jun-26) → ₹3,845.0 cr (Sep-26) — execution outran new awards in Q2 FY27. And although H1 FY27 consolidated revenue was ₹694 cr (+78%) with EBITDA ₹105 cr (+128%, 15% margin), **Q2 PAT was ₹9 cr against ₹18 cr, down 50%, while Q2 EBITDA rose 78%** — something below EBITDA took the quarter, and the press release does not say what. Book is about 2.8x the H1 revenue run rate annualised.

`ob_tracker.py` priced it: **entry ₹110.55 on the 14-Aug-2026 trigger day → ₹81.70 today, –26.1% over 96 days**, best close since only +6.1%, market cap **₹357 cr**. So a confirmed +70% order-book jump that the market has de-rated by a quarter — which is the setup this lane exists to surface. It was **not published as a card today** for a stated reason rather than a judgement on merit: the Action's signals landed at 19:57 IST after research had closed, and no dossier, no X sweep and no ValuePickr sweep were done, so a card would have breached the playbook's own research standard. **It is the top order-book candidate for the next run.**

### 2. Admach Systems Ltd (BSE 544669) — NOT A JUMP, recorded so it is never re-checked

The screen showed ₹51.44 cr → ₹78.39 cr, +52.4%. **The latest figure is fully confirmed**: the 14-Nov-2026 press release states *"Current Order Book: ₹78.39 Crore (including GST)"* in its highlights and again in the MD's quote, and the covering letter's subject line is *"Submission of Press Release pertaining to Total Order Book of the Company"* — unambiguously the company-wide total.

**The year-ago leg fails on three counts.** (1) **The as-on date is misdated by the screen.** `orderbook.py` assigned 2025-09-30 on its 'quarter before filing' rule, but the figure comes from the 31-Dec-2025 press release's *"About Admach Systems Limited"* boilerplate — *"In FY25, the Company reported revenue of ₹5,335.82 lakhs ... and a growing order book of approx. ₹5,144 lakhs"* — which attaches it to **FY25, the year ended 31-Mar-2025**. The span is therefore **594 days**, outside the 240–480 day window the rule intends. (2) On the correct dates, +52.4% over 19.5 months is about **+30% a year**, below the bar. (3) The two figures are **not on the same basis** — ₹78.39 cr is 'including GST', the earlier figure states no basis, is qualified 'approx.' and is boilerplate rather than an order-book disclosure. Verdict **NOT A JUMP**, `qualifies: false`, `true_yoy_pct: null`. For context the book is **0.95x** trailing revenue of ₹82.66 cr.

**A fetch trap worth recording.** The year-ago PDF is no longer on `AttachLive` — that URL returns BSE's "The Page you are looking for has been moved" HTML, which PyMuPDF parses happily as a two-page document of navigation links. It had to be re-fetched from `AttachHis`. Any check reading an older filing by a stored AttachLive URL will silently get an error page; the giveaways are a tiny file (8 KB here) and body text about 'Pre Open / Equity Market Watch'. The same applies on NSE: the queue stores `nsearchives.nseindia.**in**` URLs, which are unreachable from this sandbox, while the identical path on `nsearchives.nseindia.**com**` returns 200 — that substitution is what made the NSE-only filings readable at all.

`ob_tracker.py` re-run at 21:41 IST: **35 qualifying jump rows priced, 0 carried forward stale**, plus 25 order-wins rows, 0 stale. Admach is absent from the tracker, correctly, because `qualifies` is false.

updates_sweep:
**Corrected: a complete queue for today DOES exist — the Action built it at 19:56 IST, and the sweep below uses it.** `docs/ideas/updates_queue.json` is built **2026-11-18 19:56 IST** for **83 ideas**, with **82 `complete` and 1 `SUSPECT`**. An earlier draft of this log said the queue could not be had at all; that was true of this sandbox and false of the day.

**SECOND READER: 1 MISS, AND PER THE STANDING RULE THAT IS A FAILURE TO FIX RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE.** `second_reader_misses: 1`, `second_reader_problems: []`. The miss: the whole-market NSE feed carried a **'Press Release' for VEEFIN dated 2026-11-18 that the per-company NSE read did not return**, which is why `2026-10-26-VEEFIN` is the one SUSPECT idea. The substance is covered — that press release is the Veefin AI OS launch, written up below from the BSE copy of the same document — but **the per-company NSE read for this company dropped a filing the daily feed had**, and that is a reading defect in `updates.py`, not a data accident. It needs diagnosing in the per-company NSE announcement call for VEEFIN; it is reported here rather than fixed because the routine must not edit `scripts/ideas/*.py`.

**Why this run could not build the queue itself, read from the script rather than inferred.** `www.nseindia.com` answers **403** at this sandbox's egress proxy, so every per-company NSE read fails, and `updates.py` guards exactly that case — `if NSE_CALLS['ok'] == 0 and NSE_CALLS['fail'] > 0: ... sys.exit(3)` — with the queue write placed **after** the guard. A run from here can therefore never produce a queue, by design, because a queue built without NSE would silently drop every NSE-only filing.

**A process error of this run, stated because it cost about 90 minutes.** `updates.py --selftest` was started at 19:53 IST wrapped in `timeout 5400` and the timeout killed it at **idea 55 of 83** (RC=124). Nothing was lost but time — the write and the SELFTEST assertions both run only after all 83 ideas are read — **and no SELFTEST verdict was obtained in this run, which the playbook requires.** It was restarted detached, then deliberately stopped once the exit-3 guard was read, since a second pass could not have written the queue either. Over its 55 ideas the killed pass measured 40 SUSPECT and 15 complete, every SUSPECT being `NSE <window> failed`.

**The sweep, done in two passes.**

*Pass one, before the Action landed:* a throwaway BSE-only gap reader was written in the scratchpad (not in `scripts/ideas/`) over BSE's whole-market day lists for **2026-11-14 to 2026-11-18** — already cached complete by the scan and the order-book refresh, each with `rows` equal to BSE's own `reported` count (2,326 / 239 / 1,073 / 755 / 646) — matching every row to our ideas by BSE scrip code. It found **110 filings, 95 non-routine, 15 filed today on an already-published card**, and covers only the **74 of 86 ideas that have a BSE scrip**.

*Pass two, on the Action's queue:* **31 ideas carry new non-routine items, 63 items in all.** Diffing those against what was already logged showed the BSE-only pass had missed the NSE-only filings for names with no BSE scrip — exactly the gap pass one had flagged — and two of them were material.

**Cross-checking against what was already on the cards mattered more than either pass.** **44 updates dated 2026-11-13 or later were already written by yesterday's run**, which had covered 13–17 November thoroughly despite its own stale queue — INDOBORAX's Kronox pledge, DBL's completion certificate, DYCL's director resignation, PARAGMILK's warrant allotment, TEXRAIL's two 14-Nov orders, MARKOLINES' three orders, MOREPENLAB's rating upgrade, ADVAIT's GETCO order, and the H1/Q2 results of HSIL, RECODE, MANAKSTEEL, DEEDEV, VRAJ and HILINFRA among them. note:
**THREE CARDS FROM THE FILINGS LANE, ONE CONFIRMED ORDER-BOOK JUMP BANKED FOR TOMORROW, AND A RUN THAT HAD TO CORRECT ITSELF HALFWAY THROUGH.**

The ideas-feeds Action had been cancelled at its 90-minute cap on 13, 16 and 17 November, so this run started by treating the committed panels as four trading days stale and the government lane as dark — both true of the files it read at 19:43 IST. **Then today's Action succeeded and landed at 19:57 IST**, mid-run, with fresh prices, a real PIB read and a complete updates queue. The run merged origin/main, kept its own better scan (613 of 619 rows read at 19:44 against the Action's 591 of 592 at 19:19, which is what caught BLS Polymers' 18:45–19:20 results), took the Action's version of everything it could not fetch itself, and redid the commodity and updates lanes. Several statements in the first draft of this log were wrong and are corrected rather than quietly dropped.

**Lane by lane.** GOVERNMENT: the lane ran from Actions and kept **0 of 41** releases — a measured quiet day, not a failure. The one unmapped release (Export Promotion Mission, ₹25,060 cr) was assessed and rejected on the measured history: an export subsidy widens support, it does not become somebody's order book, which is the PM Surya Ghar pattern that underperformed outright. COMMODITY: the panel **was** fresh (spot today, trade month 2026-09), 40 of 53 groups above the bar — and no card, because the strongest groups are input costs for converters, which the playbook says to use as red flags. **Polyethylene and polypropylene at +10.00 is the actual input for two of today's three cards**, a sharper read than the generic crude link the cards were first written with. FILING: 15 candidates, four opened to their filings, three published.

**What the three cards share is that the trigger the scan fired on is not why any of them was published**, and each card says so. INDO SMC's ₹18.25 cr order is 4.4% of a trailing year's sales from a company that has filed eight order intimations in 240 days — both of the weakest buckets in the measured order study. Glen's results flatter: profit outgrew revenue only because interest and depreciation fell, while EBITDA margin slipped 141 bps, and its most important filing of the day slipped the Howrah plant a third time. BLS Polymers has the best business of the three on every cash and return metric and is published at **low** confidence anyway, because eleven trading sessions of listed life, no transcript, no guidance, no utilisation and no comparable peer is not enough evidence to carry 51x trailing earnings at an all-time high.

**The most valuable work today was reading the filings properly rather than the press releases.** Opening the results documents' segment notes, balance sheets and cash-flow statements changed all three cards materially: INDO SMC turns out to be **76.8% CT/PT transformers**, not the SMC-and-FRP business its call describes, with **operating cash flow negative in every period on record** (–₹34.77 cr in FY26 against ₹32.38 cr of reported PAT); Glen's **operating cash flow swung ₹65 cr** to +₹28.56 cr while ₹8.61 cr of new borrowing part-funded capex against management's "internal resources" claim; and BLS Polymers' margin jump is the polymer division's **own** (PBIT margin 10.4% → 17.9%), not the mix artefact first attributed, while its capacity ceiling corrects from ₹808 cr to ~₹702 cr once only polymer-segment revenue is divided by manufacturing capacity. One X post this run had marked wrong turned out to be **right** about INDO SMC's shape; that is corrected on the card under its own heading.

**Banked rather than published: Ganesh Infraworld**, a CONFIRMED +70.0% order-book jump (₹2,262.3 cr → ₹3,845 cr on clean 30-Sep dates, both read this run), market cap ₹357 cr, and **down 26.1% since the trigger filing**. It was not written up because the Action's signals arrived after research had closed and no dossier or sweeps were done — a thin card would have breached the research standard. It is the top candidate for the next run.

**Two process errors of this run, logged so they are not repeated:** the updates sweep was wrapped in a timeout shorter than the job needs and was killed at idea 55 of 83, costing ~90 minutes and the SELFTEST verdict; and step 0's `pip install pymupdf` installs into Python 3.13 while `python3` is 3.11, so PDF reading silently failed until `python3 -m pip` was used.
data_problems: **THE ideas-feeds ACTION SUCCEEDED TODAY, BUT THE 90-MINUTE CAP REMAINS THE PIPELINE'S BIGGEST STRUCTURAL RISK.** Run 44313598476 landed at 19:57 IST (128 files, 0 refused, only `wpi` failed) in ~61 minutes. The three preceding trading days — runs 43433543004 (13-Nov), 43875640839 (16-Nov) and 44092608136 (17-Nov) — were each cancelled at exactly 90 minutes with step 19 'Order-book ledger refresh' still running (61 minutes on its own on 17-Nov, 13:48:52Z → 14:50:09Z), so step 26 'Commit the feeds' was skipped and a complete day's feeds was discarded three times. The successful runs took 62 and ~61 minutes against the 90-minute cap, so the margin is one slow BSE evening. **Needs a change to `.github/workflows/ideas-feeds.yml`, outside this routine's scope:** raise `timeout-minutes`, and/or split the order-book refresh into its own workflow, and/or move the commit earlier so completed feeds land even when a later step is killed.

**THE SECOND READER FOUND ONE FILING THE PER-COMPANY READ MISSED, AND THAT IS A READING DEFECT TO FIX.** Today's queue (built 19:56 IST, 83 ideas) reports `second_reader_misses: 1`: the whole-market NSE feed carried a **'Press Release' for VEEFIN dated 2026-11-18** that the per-company NSE read did not return, making `2026-10-26-VEEFIN` the only SUSPECT idea of 83. The substance is covered (the Veefin AI OS launch, written up from the BSE copy), but the per-company NSE announcement read for that company dropped a filing the daily feed had. Reported rather than fixed because the routine must not edit `scripts/ideas/*.py`.

**THE SELFTEST DID NOT RUN, SO THE 'NO FILING MAY BE MISSED' GUARANTEE IS UNVERIFIED THIS RUN.** `updates.py --selftest` was started at 19:53 IST wrapped in `timeout 5400` and killed at idea 55 of 83 (RC=124); the SELFTEST assertions run only after all 83 ideas are read. It was restarted detached and then deliberately stopped once the script's `sys.exit(3)` guard was read — with every NSE call failing from this sandbox, no second pass could have written the queue or reached the assertions either. **This was a process error of this run**, and the lesson is that on this sandbox `updates.py` is a ~2.5-hour job that cannot succeed at all, so it should be run only to harvest its per-idea read, or skipped in favour of the committed queue.

**NSE IS BLOCKED FROM THIS SANDBOX, WHICH IS WHY THE QUEUE CANNOT BE BUILT HERE AT ALL.** `www.nseindia.com` answers 403 at the egress proxy. `updates.py` guards exactly this — `if NSE_CALLS['ok'] == 0 and NSE_CALLS['fail'] > 0: ... sys.exit(3)` — with the queue write after the guard, by design, because a queue built without NSE would silently drop every NSE-only filing. **A workaround found in this run and worth keeping:** the queue stores `nsearchives.nseindia.**in**` document URLs, which are unreachable here, while the identical path on `nsearchives.nseindia.**com**` returns 200. That substitution is what made today's NSE-only filings — including Viviana's rights-issue board meeting and Supreme Power's order — readable.

**EVERY COMMODITY PRICE SOURCE EXCEPT THE BSE-HOSTED ONES WAS BLOCKED FROM THIS SANDBOX, THOUGH THE ACTION GOT MOST OF THEM.** From here: `spot.py` fetched 0 commodities (all 8 westmetall series and businessinsider failed) and left `spot.json`/`spot_series.json` unchanged, correctly; `india_spot.py` had metalbook, ibja, rubber, sugar, fuel, cai, spices, guidechem and trading-economics all FAIL with 'previous rows kept', only `nmdc` (2 rows), `minsteel` (3, re-published from the committed file) and `moil` (3) working, all BSE-hosted, and **0 history rows appended**; `minsteel.py`, `wpi.py` and `trade.py` all left their files unchanged. The Action's build replaced most of this: `spot_date` is now 2026-11-18 19:16 IST and `trade_month` 2026-09. **What is still genuinely missing is WPI** — `wpi_month` remains **2026-04, seven months old**, because the WPI builder was the Action's one failed step and eaindustry.nic.in is blocked here too. The WPI evidence behind Crude oil, Silver and Sulphuric acid has not moved since April and must not be read as a new move.

**THE SCAN'S FILING COUNT IS A FLOOR, NOT THE DAY.** This run's scan (kept over the Action's in the merge) read 613 rows against BSE's own `announcements_reported` 619, so `announcements_capped` is TRUE: a page came back six rows short and the rows kept are the newest. Read at 19:44 IST, same-day, so filings uploaded later are absent — BLS Polymers' own results came in at 18:45–19:20 and only just made it. The Action's scan was worse on both counts (591 of 592, read 19:19, 14 candidates against 15), which is why this run's version was kept. Never quote 613 as the day's filings.

**`orderbook.py` MISDATED AN ORDER-BOOK FIGURE EMBEDDED IN BOILERPLATE.** For Admach Systems it assigned 2025-09-30 to a figure the source sentence attaches to FY25 (31-Mar-2025), using its 'quarter before filing' rule on a press release dated 31-Dec-2025 whose ₹5,144 lakh order book sits inside an 'In FY25, the Company reported...' sentence in the About-the-company block. That turned a ~30%-a-year change into a reported +52.4% 'year-on-year'. Recorded as NOT A JUMP with the reasoning on the row. The rule is right most of the time; it is wrong when the amount is inside a retrospective sentence, and a guard on 'In FY..' phrasing would catch it.

**A BSE ARCHIVE TRAP THAT SILENTLY RETURNS AN ERROR PAGE AS A PDF.** The year-ago Admach filing is no longer on `AttachLive`; that URL returns BSE's 'The Page you are looking for has been moved' HTML, which PyMuPDF parses happily as a two-page document of navigation links. It had to be re-fetched from `AttachHis`. Any check reading an older filing by a stored AttachLive URL will get an error page rather than a failure; the giveaways are a tiny file (8 KB here) and body text about 'Pre Open / Equity Market Watch'.

**THE X SWEEP COULD NOT READ A SINGLE POST DIRECTLY.** `cdn.syndication.twimg.com:443` was refused at the egress proxy (`connect_rejected`), so the playbook's method — fetch a post by id and read its `text`/`note_tweet` JSON — was unavailable for all three researched names. Every gist in every `x_posts` entry and every quote in every `social` section comes from a domain-restricted WebSearch snippet, which is weaker evidence, and each card says so. WebSearch itself worked and the sweep still produced 12 primary-verified data points and 2 contradictions, so this degraded the sweep rather than stopping it.

**THE VALUEPICKR SWEEP DID NOT RUN AT ALL.** `forum.valuepickr.com:443` was refused at the egress proxy, so neither `search.json?q=` nor `raw/<id>?page=N` was reachable for any name. A domain-restricted WebSearch found no dedicated thread for INDO SMC, Glen Industries or BLS Polymers — but it did find BLS Polymers named in passing inside the DDev Plastiks thread, which **could not be opened to check for more**. All three cards record this as 'not checked properly', never as 'nothing on ValuePickr'.

**A DEFECT IN THIS ROUTINE'S OWN STEP 0.** `python3 -c "import fitz" 2>/dev/null || pip install --quiet pymupdf` cannot work on this image: `pip` belongs to Python 3.13 and `python3` on PATH is 3.11.18, so pymupdf 2.1 and xlrd installed into `/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages` while `import fitz` kept failing under 3.11 — pip even reported 'Requirement already satisfied' on the retry. `minsteel.py` crashed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fitz'`. Fixed in-run with `python3 -m pip install --quiet pymupdf xlrd`; the prompt's step 0 should use `python3 -m pip`. Note also that PyMuPDF 2.1 warns `fitz` is deprecated in favour of `import pymupdf` — a future break for every builder here, not a current one.

**THE SHIP-IT PAGE GATE COULD ONLY BE RUN HALFWAY, AND IT CAUGHT FIVE REAL DEFECTS ANYWAY.** `docs/ideas.html` is auth-gated and renders 'This page is private' without Supabase, which is blocked here, so the cards could not be seen rendered in a browser. Instead `md()`, `inl()`, `esc()` and `table()` were extracted from `docs/ideas.html` itself and the cards, the 13 updates and the whole run log were run through the real implementations under Node. That found and fixed: three lines where a blockquote-to-bold conversion had nested `**` inside `**`; one `*Audited\**` escape leaving a stray marker; and — the genuinely useful one — **a literal `**` inside backticks breaks `inl()`, because code ticks are substituted before bold, so the stray marker swallows the rest of the paragraph**. Final pass: 52 tables, 1,211 cells on the cards, 13 updates and the run log all at **0 defects**, every markdown link resolved to an anchor, no stray pipes, nothing unsafe. All 27 `docs/ideas/*.json` and both `.json.gz` verified to parse. **What was NOT verified: the cards' appearance, dark/light rendering and 375px layout in a real browser.**
